blocks.h: Which water each standard asks for
blocks.intro: None of these is Purified Water. Purified Water is held to ≤ 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C (USP <645> stage 1), with no endotoxin limit.
cols: How it differs from Purified Water
rows: Critical water
Fewer ions removed, far tighter on microbes, plus an endotoxin limit: < 10 µS/cm, < 10 colony-forming units (CFU)/mL, < 10 endotoxin units/mL
ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023; CSA Z314:23
Utility water
Looser: < 500 µS/cm, < 500 CFU/mL. As the final rinse after high-level disinfection: < 10 CFU/mL and < 10 endotoxin units/mL
ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023
Type II reagent water
Tighter on ions and organic carbon: < 1 µS/cm at 25 °C, total organic carbon < 50 µg/L
ASTM D1193-24; values from D1193-06
Type III reagent water
Tighter on ions than Type II, looser on organic carbon: < 0.25 µS/cm at 25 °C, total organic carbon < 200 µg/L. Not a purity ladder
ASTM D1193-24; values from D1193-06
Clinical laboratory reagent water
Defined for medical laboratories; an analyzer maker's specification governs that analyzer's feed
CLSI GP40 5th ed.
Type I reagent water
Made at the bench by a point-of-use polisher fed from the loop, not by a central loop
ASTM D1193-24

items.d: Written to your water management program and approved before any test runs.
Drawings, materials, instruments and calibration checked as installed. Good manufacturing practice (GMP) sites call it installation qualification.
Flows, alarms, controls and sanitization tested against the protocol. GMP sites call it operational qualification.
Hospitals: bacteria and endotoxin at loop out, loop return and each outlet. Laboratories: verification to CLSI GP40.
Critical water: conductivity daily after the last treatment step. Bacteria and endotoxin monthly at loop out, loop return and each outlet.

items.q: Do you supply water for hospital reprocessing?
items.a: Yes: [hospital water scope]. Reprocessing water is critical water under ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023 and CSA Z314:23, a different grade from Purified Water.
No. Dialysis water systems are licensed as medical devices, and we do not make them. No Water for Injection, pure steam or stainless steel systems.

items.q: Can the loop be disinfected with hot water?
items.a: Not routinely. Natural PP is rated 0 to 80 °C, and its pressure rating falls as it heats. Any hot-water cycle stays inside the PP maker's pressure–temperature curve for its hours: [maximum loop sanitization temperature for PP, °C]. A hot-held loop needs a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) or stainless loop [whether we quote PVDF].

items.q: Can you supply Type I water?
items.a: No, not from a central loop. ASTM D1193-24 Type I comes from a point-of-use polisher at the bench, fed from the loop. Send the polisher maker's feed specification, and the loop is designed to it.

items.q: Can one plant serve reprocessing and the laboratory?
items.a: Yes, or two plants; your consultant decides. A shared plant feeds separate storage, each held to its own grade. Separate plants let one be disinfected while the other runs.

items.q: Can the changeover happen in an occupied building?
items.a: Yes. The changeover plan sets shutdown windows, temporary water and isolation with your facilities team and contractor.
